calls.head: Heavyweight bout
calls.body: The Oilers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kraken are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We think the Kraken win this one.
calls.call: The Kraken keep the Oilers’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).
calls.nums: Edmonton 7th for chance quality (a 6.5% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Seattle 3rd for preventing dangerous shots

calls.head: The Kraken can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Oilers’ power play is the league’s best, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.9 expected goals per 60.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 72% chance, and they delivered.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Seattle hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Seattle is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 61 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 113 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: The Oilers get past the Kraken
paras: Owen Michaels struck first for the Oilers early in the first. Bobby McMann tied it on the power play midway through the second. Leon Draisaitl put the Oil ahead for good with 2:27 left. Connor McDavid sealed it into the empty net with 1:05 left.
The Oilers drove the play, outshooting the Kraken 26-20, and the scoreboard caught up. Devon Levi made 19 saves for the Oilers, and Philipp Grubauer stopped 23 of 25.
Ryan Lindgren and Trent Frederic fought midway through the first. Mattias Ekholm and Brandon Montour picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Oilers improved to 2-0-1, and the Kraken fell to 1-1-0.

items.text: Leon Draisaitl extended his point streak against Seattle to nine games.
The Oilers have beaten the Kraken four straight times, going back to 2025-26.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
